stem: Which infection-prevention activity best reflects CDC guidance on performance monitoring and feedback?

options.A: Regularly monitor adherence to recommended infection-prevention practices and provide feedback to staff to improve performance.
options.B: Measure infection-prevention adherence only after a major outbreak.
options.C: Avoid giving staff feedback because performance data should remain confidential from the care team.
options.D: Replace observation and monitoring with annual policy review alone.

rationale: CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices include monitoring adherence to recommended practices and providing feedback to health-care personnel to improve performance.
educational_objective: Recognize monitoring plus feedback as a core infection-prevention performance-improvement practice.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices for Safe Healthcare Delivery in All Settings
source_claim_supported: CDC recommends monitoring adherence to infection-prevention practices and providing feedback to improve performance.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection-prevention quality monitoring
correction_summary: Rebuilt the item around the exact CDC Core Practice of adherence monitoring and feedback.
